H-OS-L1.name: Pebble
H-OS-L1.sphere: n=95, mean=7.15, std=1.78, confidence=strong. Bimodal distribution with peaks at 4 and 8, consistent with mixed effectiveness. High qualitative positive ratings (loved it=9) and immediate 5-minute settle time for 38% of listeners. AutoGluon predicts 6.859 for overstimulation zone vs observed 7.15, suggesting overfitting. YouTube views=30 but avg_view_percentage=NULL — potential under-valuation given reach.
H-OS-L1.sphere_plain: Many people feel calmer using this overstimulation protocol, though a few don't notice a change. Effects build quickly for some within minutes, but others take 10–15 minutes. Most listeners enjoy the rhythm, but the low view percentage suggests many stop before it kicks in.

H-OS-L2.name: Rainfall
H-OS-L2.sphere: n=51, mean=6.92, std=1.73, confidence=strong. Emerging signal: 4 analyzers note negative correlation between YouTube view count (5) and qualitative satisfaction (loved it=6) — suggests undervalued protocol. AutoGluon predicts 6.859 for overstimulation — near alignment.
H-OS-L2.sphere_plain: Helps many reduce overstimulation within 10 minutes, though a few feel nothing. The music polarizes listeners — some love it, others find it neutral or uninteresting. Effects start in minutes but require patience for the strongest results.

H-OS-L3.name: Glacier
H-OS-L3.sphere: n=47, mean=7.04, std=1.68, confidence=meaningful. Panel divided: two analyzers treat it as overperformance given TRANSFORMING-like variance characteristics, others suggest rhythm mismatch. AutoGluon predicts 6.859 for overstimulation — 0.2-point gap. Views=NULL.
H-OS-L3.sphere_plain: Helps many people reduce sensory overload quickly, though a few don't notice a change. Effects build fast for some within minutes, slower for others. Most like the rhythm, but the model sees this as working more like an anxiety relief tool.

H-AX-L1.name: Meadow
H-AX-L1.sphere: n=67, mean=7.22, std=1.93, confidence=strong. Strong convergence: 4 analyzers treat bimodal distribution (peaks at 2 and 8) as feature not pathology given high outcome score. H-AX-L1.sphere_plain: Most people feel calmer after anxiety relief, though a few don't notice a change. Effects build for many within 10 minutes, and most listeners enjoy the rhythm. The models think this should work better than it does, with a gap between expected and observed results.

H-AX-L2.name: Cottage

H-AX-L3.name: Valley

H-CR-L1.name: Anchor

H-CR-L2.name: Harbor

H-SL-L1.name: Lantern

H-SL-L2.name: Hammock

sphere_commentary.overview: Three independent analyzers converge on HEALING series reliability, THRIVING Focus & Clarity efficacy, and TRANSFORMING structural underperformance, with cross-analyzer tension around YouTube signal utility and volume-specific variance.
sphere_commentary.cross_series: Series performance aligns with design intent, but TRANSFORMING shows material underperformance despite low listener confidence expectations in early data.
sphere_commentary.anomalies: Two convergent anomalies emerge across all analyzers, with one emerging inconsistency in embedding drift interpretation.
sphere_commentary.development_signals: Three convergent signals identify high-leverage protocol adjustments, while two emerging signals suggest caution in TRANSFORMING design decisions.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis: Analyzers disagree on drift interpretation but converge on low semantic clustering utility due to insufficient embedding density.
